topic.title: Q-Function Learning, Conservatism, and Critic Stability
topic.overview: Q-functions estimate the expected return from taking an action and then following a policy. This topic studies how to learn these estimates with neural approximators, how to control overestimation, and how critic structure affects the policy it trains. Offline datasets, large action spaces, and target-update choices introduce different sources of instability.
topic.whyItMatters: A policy can exploit inaccurate values for actions poorly represented in its data, so accurate fitting on observed transitions is insufficient. Conservative estimates address this risk, while smooth critic geometry matters when value gradients determine continuous actions. These goals can conflict with aggressive value maximization.
topic.evolution: Early work in 1992 studies neural Q-learning with hidden-unit restarts. Conservative Q-learning in 2020 adds a value regularizer to address offline distribution shift. Later representatives investigate distributional estimates and large action spaces; a 2026 critic-centered approach regularizes the action-gradient field to reduce erratic policies while retaining useful curvature.
openQuestions: How can conservatism adapt to the actual coverage of an offline dataset?
Which critic regularizers improve physical action smoothness without obscuring important value differences?

papers.tldr: Partial linear realizability of policy values still permits computationally hard reinforcement learning problems under the paper's studied policy classes and complexity assumptions.

papers.title: Continuous Q-Score Matching: Diffusion Guided Reinforcement Learning for Continuous-Time Control
papers.tldr: CQSM links continuous-time Q-functions to diffusion policy scores, enabling policy improvement while preserving action evaluation without time discretization.

papers.title: $Q\sharp$: Provably Optimal Distributional RL for LLM Post-Training
papers.tldr: Q-sharp learns regularized action values for LLM post-training, combining conditional optimality guarantees with stronger math reasoning and smaller reference-policy divergence.

papers.title: Risk-Averse Total-Reward Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: A Q-learning algorithm learns optimal stationary policies for risk-averse, undiscounted total-reward objectives with convergence and performance guarantees.

papers.title: ShiQ: Bringing back Bellman to LLMs
papers.tldr: ShiQ derives Bellman-based losses that turn language-model logits into useful Q-value estimates for off-policy, token-level learning.

papers.title: Value Improved Actor Critic Algorithms
papers.tldr: Value improvement adds greedier updates to actor-critic value estimation while keeping acting-policy changes gradual, improving or matching reported TD3 and SAC performance.

papers.title: Accelerating Q-learning through Efficient Value-Sharing across Actions
papers.tldr: A parameter-free network layer accelerates action-value learning by sharing values across actions and learning a smaller-norm representation.

papers.title: Chunk-Guided Q-Learning
papers.tldr: CGQ uses a chunk-based critic to guide single-step value learning, reducing accumulated errors while retaining fine-grained decisions.

papers.title: Clipped Q-Learning: Your Value Clipping Is Secretly A Robust Operator
papers.tldr: Clipped Q-learning has a theoretical interpretation as learning robustly against specific adverse changes in transition probabilities.

papers.title: Commit to the Bit: Reactive Reinforcement Learning Done Right
papers.tldr: Committed Q-learning learns an optimal reactive policy under a weaker structural assumption by retaining its chosen action until the observed feature changes.

papers.title: Corruption-Tolerant Asynchronous Q-Learning with Near-Optimal Rates
papers.tldr: Robust asynchronous Q-learning achieves near-optimal finite-time guarantees with an added error term tied to reward corruption.

papers.title: Debiased Model-based Representations for Sample-efficient Continuous Control
papers.tldr: DR.Q improves dynamics-informed representations and replay sampling, matching or surpassing strong continuous-control baselines with a single hyperparameter setting.

papers.title: Direct Flow Q-Learning
papers.tldr: Direct Flow Q-Learning trains iterative flow policies with terminal value guidance, avoiding both backpropagation through time and distillation.

papers.title: Frictional Q-Learning
papers.tldr: Frictional Q-Learning uses action-support geometry to reduce unstable value extrapolation toward poorly observed actions.

papers.title: Learning to Bet for Horizon-Aware Anytime-Valid Testing
papers.tldr: A learned betting policy adapts anytime-valid tests to deadlines using theoretical guidance on when to bet more or less aggressively.

papers.title: Multi-timescale Reinforcement Learning by Value Reconstruction
papers.tldr: A multi-timescale critic reconstructs rewards and adaptively combines Q-values to improve short- and long-term decision-making.

papers.title: Reward Redistribution for CVaR MDPs using a Bellman Operator on L-infinity
papers.tldr: A new augmented-state CVaR formulation supplies dense rewards and contraction properties for convergent risk-averse learning algorithms.

papers.title: Scalable Reinforcement Learning via Adaptive Batch Scaling
papers.tldr: Adaptive Batch Scaling increases batch size as policy behavior stabilizes, enabling stronger scaling results with larger networks on ALE.

papers.title: Stabilizing the Q-Gradient Field for Policy Smoothness in Actor-Critic Methods
papers.tldr: PAVE smooths actor-critic policies by stabilizing the critic’s action gradients while preserving curvature and leaving the actor unchanged.

papers.title: The Role of Target Update Frequencies in Q-Learning
papers.tldr: A tabular Q-learning analysis shows that geometrically decreasing target update frequency avoids the sample overhead of constant schedules.

papers.title: TQL: Scaling Q-Functions with Transformers by Preventing Attention Collapse
papers.tldr: TQL controls attention entropy to prevent collapse, enabling larger transformer value functions to improve reinforcement-learning performance.
